text:
Dylan Guenther scored 40 goals last season, and the early read on this one is that Utah's power play is carrying him while his even-strength game catches up. Nine of his 12 points have come with the man advantage, which is why CBS Sports called him a "Power-play machine" this week. At five on five the picture is thinner: Utah's share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is 7.4 points worse with him on the ice than without him, and over his last ten games he has four points where our numbers expected about seven and a half.

None of that looks like a player in trouble. His own chances per hour are up a little on last season, his finishing sits right around what those chances deserve, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 92nd percentile last season for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net. Our projection's middle case is another 35 goals over the rest of the season. What we'd watch is five on five: when that turns, the points will come in bunches.
headline: The power play is doing the heavy lifting
